questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Norway since we can speak together, which is a large advantage when being in the hospital. I know fellow students who have been to more exotic destinations without the same academic outcome since they did not understand the initial clinical examination preformed at the hospital.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the hospital I went to, Lovisenberg, the only exchange students were the two of us from Copenhagen, which I think is a shame, since the experience of being in exchange is also to meet students from around the world or Europe.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. I had already mailed with the doctor I was supposed to meet with the first day.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *

Additional comments
questions.answer: It would have been nice to have a student from Norway to show me around town.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live together with someone from your destination.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As far as I am concerned, it was only possible to rent a student house for a full semester, even though I was only there for three months.
